newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Norway finance minister sees EMU cooperation - paper.
newsitem.headline: Norway finance minister sees EMU cooperation - paper.

text.p: Norwegian Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg said in an interview published on Wednesday that he could envisage cooperation between non-EU member Norway and Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
"I am for monetary union because it will lead to currency stability in Europe," Stoltenberg was quoted as saying by Swedish financial newspaper FinansTidningen.

"I can see cooperation with the future euro bloc," said Stoltenberg, who switched from the energy portfolio to the finance ministry last October under the new Labour government of Prime Minister Thoerbjoern Jagland.
Former premier Gro Harlem Brundtland has said the crown should somehow be coupled with the single European currency to be created under EMU, due to start in 1999.
Norway, which rejected membership of the EU in a 1994 referendum, has a managed float for the crown and seeks to maintain a stable exchange rate against European currencies.
However, the Norwegian crown has rocketed to 52-month highs against the German mark since December on the back of the strong oil-driven Norwegian economy.
Next year's budget surplus is projected at 55.4 billion crowns thanks to high oil prices. The projected surplus amounts to 6.5 percent of GDP, which means Norway would easily qualify for EMU.
The Maastrict convergence criteria for joining EMU require that a budget deficit does not fall below three percent of GDP.
Stoltenberg said Norway could afford to stay outside the EU but for political reasons it was important for the country to join.
"I don't think it will take much longer before Norway holds a new referendum on the EU," he said, but gave no timetable.
The government has said the question of EU membership is dead for now but could be revived after the year 2000.
